task.title: metric carries a rounded-up value into quetta and into scientific notation without an extra digit
task.body:
Why: https://github.com/python-humanize/humanize/issues/423 ; src/humanize/number.py:596 skips the rounding carry when `exponent >= 30`. On b519e48 `metric(9.996e30)` returns '10.00 Q', `metric(9.996e31)` returns '100.0 Q' and `metric(9.996e32)` returns '1000 Q', while `metric(9999)` correctly gives '10.0 k'.
Outcome: `humanize.metric(value, unit="", precision=3)` applies the same rounding carry for values in the quetta range as for every other prefix, keeping `precision` significant digits: `metric(9.996e30) == '10.0 Q'`, `metric(9.996e31) == '100 Q'`. A value in the quetta range that rounds up to 1e33 is shown in scientific notation, the same as `metric(1e33)`: `metric(9.996e32) == '1.00 x 10³³'`. Unchanged: `metric(9999) == '10.0 k'`, `metric(1e30) == '1.00 Q'`, `metric(9.99e32) == '999 Q'`, `metric(1e33) == '1.00 x 10³³'`.
Proof: add tests to tests/test_number.py.

spec: `humanize.metric(value, unit="", precision=3)` applies the same rounding carry for values in the quetta range as for every other prefix, keeping `precision` significant digits: `metric(9.996e30) == '10.0 Q'`, `metric(9.996e31) == '100 Q'`. A value in the quetta range that rounds up to 1e33 is shown in scientific notation, the same as `metric(1e33)`: `metric(9.996e32) == '1.00 x 10³³'`. Unchanged: `metric(9999) == '10.0 k'`, `metric(1e30) == '1.00 Q'`, `metric(9.99e32) == '999 Q'`, `metric(1e33) == '1.00 x 10³³'`.
install: python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/python -m pip install -q babel -e '.[tests]' && .venv/bin/pybabel --quiet compile --directory src/humanize/locale --domain humanize
